title: NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Contents Claim Payments
content:
Contents claim payments on the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) are issued by the claims desk on the policy's claim that carries its latest adjuster report, for that claim's date of loss, and a contents payment is paid to the insured alone.

**When a contents payment is fixed.** A contents payment on a claim is fixed only after the claim file carries a signed and sworn contents proof of loss received after the claim's latest adjuster report that measures a contents loss. As long as the claim file shows no contents proof of loss with a received date later than that report, the contents payment on the claim is not fixed.

## Capability

Issuing a contents claim payment books one payment item for the contents coverage on a flood claim under a General Property Form or RCBAP policy, to the named insured alone, dated the day it is issued, with a newly assigned payment reference, and adds it to the net claim money paid on the policy. The customer can then be told the amount and the payment reference.

## Invocation

The tool is `issue_contents_claim_payment_a4dbf5ac`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it, then calls it; each call issues one payment item.

## Parameters

1. `nfipcom_policy_id` — the reference number of the General Property Form or RCBAP policy the claim is made under, as returned by the policy lookup for the customer.
2. `claim_number` — the claim number the payment is issued under, copied character for character as it appears on the claim file or as the customer states it.
3. `date_of_loss` — the date the flood loss occurred on that claim, YYYY-MM-DD.
4. `payment_amount` — the amount of this contents payment item, in USD, positive, 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-up to the cent.

There is no payee parameter: the payee of a contents payment is always the insured.

## Receipt

`payment_id` (the reference of the new claim-file entry), `payment_ref` (the newly assigned payment reference), `claim_number`, `coverage_part` (always `CONTENTS`), `payment_amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `payee` (always `INSURED`) and `issued_date` (YYYY-MM-DD). The presence of `payment_ref` means the payment was issued. No error behaviour is defined.
